abstract: Platelet orientation offers a route to improve through-plane thermal transport in boron-nitride-filled silicone films, but its effect on compliance requires assessment. We compared vertically oriented and randomly dispersed platelets at 20 vol% using the same silicone formulation and cure. Orientation was assessed by cross-sectional microscopy. At 25 °C, the aligned films had a through-plane thermal conductivity of 1.8 ± 0.2 W m−1 K−1, compared with 0.9 ± 0.1 W m−1 K−1 for the randomly dispersed films. Their tensile moduli were 2.4 ± 0.3 and 2.2 ± 0.2 MPa, respectively. Values are means ± sample standard deviations for five independently prepared films per group; no statistical hypothesis tests were performed. The aligned films retained 92% of their initial conductivity after 500 bending cycles at a 5 mm radius. Thus, alignment improved the measured conductivity with a modest numerical increase in modulus under these conditions. Interfacial thermal resistance and device temperatures were not measured, and the mechanism underlying the improvement remains unresolved.
discussion:
Prolonged heating altered the extractability and mechanical response of the disulfide-containing polyester network. Increasing the treatment duration at 110 °C from 15 to 60 min increased the sol fraction after THF extraction from 8% to 19% and decreased the storage modulus at 1 Hz and 25 °C from 6.0 to 3.8 MPa. These means represent three separately prepared specimens per condition; without error estimates or statistical tests, their variability cannot be assessed. Together, the changes are consistent with network rearrangement and/or chain scission, but do not distinguish these processes. The broader low-molar-mass shoulder observed by SEC after 60 min supports a change in the soluble population. However, the polystyrene-calibrated SEC measurements describe only the soluble fraction, not the insoluble network.

The approximately unchanged DSC glass-transition temperature of 42 °C, within measurement resolution, and the absence of a resolvable FTIR ester carbonyl shift do not establish chemical stability; a constant carbonyl position does not exclude low levels of ester cleavage. An otherwise matched ester-only network and end-group analysis would help distinguish the proposed interpretations. These are future tests. Although reprocessing motivates this study, the present measurements do not establish performance over reprocessing cycles, recyclability, or long-term creep resistance.
results:
The fabricated 10-bit SAR ADC in 65 nm CMOS was characterized at room temperature with a 1.0 V supply and a sampling rate of 20 MS/s. For a 1.1 MHz sinusoidal input, the measured SNDR and SFDR were 57.2 and 69.5 dB, respectively. SNDR decreased to 54.8 dB at an input frequency of 9.7 MHz, showing lower dynamic performance at the higher input frequency. Peak DNL was +0.45/−0.38 LSB, and peak INL was +0.72/−0.66 LSB. Although five dies were characterized, these values are from one representative die and are not averages across the five dies.

The ADC core consumed 0.62 mW, including the comparator, DAC switching, and SAR logic. This power figure excludes the external reference driver and clock generator and therefore does not describe the power of the complete conversion setup. The active core occupied 0.018 mm², excluding pads. Power was not swept across temperature, so its temperature dependence remains uncharacterized. No measured advantage over prior work is established because a harmonized comparison was not performed.
